WAGES SERIES
The Wages series consists of deep, nearly level to sloping, well-drained soils on fans, footslopes and terraces on river and intermittent stream valleys. Slopes range from 0 to 8 percent. They formed in calcareous alluvium at elevations of 3000 to 3600 feet.
The vegetation is mainly western wheatgrass, big sage, cudweed sagewort, and green needlegrass. Annual precipitation is 13 to 14 inches, mean annual soil temperature is 47 to 49 degrees F., the frost free season is 105 to 115 days.
Typically, the surface layer is grayish brown loam about 6 inches thick. The subsoil is brown and light brownish gray loam and loam about 16 inches thick. The substratum is light brownish gray grading to light gray clay loam or fine sandy loam to 60 or more inches.
Permeability is moderate, the effective rooting depth is 60 or more inches. Available water holding capacity is 8 to 10 inches.
These soils are used for irrigated and dry cropland and for range.
A typical profile of Wages loam, colutivated, 350 feet south and 125 feet west of the WE corner of Sec. 31, T. 1 N., R. 38 E.
Ap 0 to 6 inches, grayish brown (10YR 5/2) loan, very dark grayish brown (10YR 3/2) moist; clods breaking to weak, medium granular structure; hard, friable, nonsticky and slightly plastic; abrupt smooth boundary.
6 to 9 inches, brown (10YR 5/3) clay loam, dark brown (10YR 3/3) moist; moderate, medium and coarse prismatic structure; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; patches of thin clay films on ped surfaces; gradual wavy boundary.
9 to 13 inches, brown (10YR 5/3) light clay loam, dark brown (10YR 3/3) moist; moderate, coarse prismatic structure; hard, friable, sticky and plastic; patches of thin clay films on ped surfaces; clear wavy boundary. (B25 is 6 to 10 inches thick)
B3ca 13 to 22 inches, light brownish bray (10YR 6/2) loam, dark grayish brown (10YR 4/2) moist; weak, coarse blocky structure; hard, friable, slightly sticky and slightly plastic; slightly effervescent; a few fine soft masses of segregated lime; clear wavy boundary.
